title: Explain the terminal ancestor when claim and show report blocked work
outcome: An agent claiming or inspecting work stranded below a terminal ancestor can identify the actual blocking ancestor and follow an admitted remedy, including when the direct parent is still open.
acceptance: For a completed root -> open parent -> open child, claim refusal and show identify the terminal ancestor and its lifecycle without describing the open direct parent as completed; CLI and MCP retain actionable navigation or a supported remedy.

The explanation distinguishes explicit blockers and prerequisites from an ancestor lifecycle barrier, preserves refusal to resume a frozen execution, and has regression coverage for both a direct terminal parent and a terminal grandparent.

completion.summary: Blocked work now names the actual terminal ancestor in claim refusals and show/readiness diagnostics, preserves the open direct parent's identity/lifecycle, and keeps independent barriers and frozen execution guards. Native direct/grandparent Rust and CLI/MCP regressions passed the full Windows gate; independent Codex/Claude whole-input review and acceptance passed. Three Low findings are tracked as independent follow-ups.
